subject: Sealed-site readiness & next steps for air-gapped Private deployment - quick check-in
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Alan Wu <alan.wu@genlab.com>, Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@genlab.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T13:02:00-04:00
Subject: Sealed-site readiness & next steps for air-gapped Private deployment - quick check-in

Hi Alan / Rafael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side and three proposed next actions so we can keep momentum toward a Q4 pilot: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- GenLab confirmed requirement for a fully air-gapped Private deployment inside your Boston lab (no egress traffic allowed; signed firmware only).
- Primary workload: real-time inference for microscopy annotation (~30 concurrent requests / low-latency per inference).
- Desired SLA during pilot: 99.5% availability, maintenance windows limited to 1x/month during off-hours.
- You want a fallback plan to Redwood Dedicated for canary/rollback in case of critical HW failure during pilot.

Open items we flagged on the call (we'll help with each):
1) Hardware inventory & physical constraints — please confirm rack U, power PDU types, and whether you can host a small 2U appliance + 1 spare node.
2) Firmware and image transfer process — we recommended signed images delivered via customer-controlled removable media (LTO or sealed USB) and verified via your HSM/KMS.
3) Offline patch cadence and acceptance testing — suggested quarterly security patches; need your acceptance test gates and rollback window.

Proposed next steps (pick days that work for you):
- Action A: Site inventory spreadsheet (attached) — Rafael, can you populate the checklist items by next Tue (2026-08-24)?
- Action B: FieldOps survey call — 30 min with your facilities lead to confirm rack clearance and UPS tolerances (Ben / Marissa to join).
- Action C: Draft the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) including Dedicated fallback triggers (we’ll send draft by EOD Wed).

Attachments: site_inventory_genlab.xlsx (inventory template), redwood-airgap-handoff-checklist.pdf (example handoff MOP).

If those are all acceptable I’ll schedule the FieldOps slot — suggest Wed 8/25 10am ET or Thu 8/26 2pm ET.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Alan Wu <alan.wu@genlab.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@genlab.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@genlab.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T17:44:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sealed-site readiness & next steps for air-gapped Private deployment - quick check-in

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the clear recap. Rafael and I reviewed the attachments after the call; a few clarifications below: 

1) Inventory: Rafael will populate the attached spreadsheet but to be explicit — rack space is tight. We have one available 4U slot and a nearby cold aisle with a single spare PDU feed. Will that suffice for the pilot (we can order an additional PDU if necessary)?

2) Signed firmware: We cannot accept USB media into the sealed lab. Our standard process is controlled LTO shipments with chain-of-custody and verification in an air-gapped staging bay. Can Redwood support LTO image ingestion and signed checksums?

3) Patch cadence: Quarterly is fine, but any security patch must be deployable via our offline MOP with a verified rollback asset. Also need a clear list of components that will be patched (OS kernels, runtime, Redwood runtime).

Procurement will need a high level BOM and a quote for appliance + 1 spare node to start the purchase path. Procurement loop: procurement@genlab.com.

We are happy to take the FieldOps call — Wed 8/25 10am ET works.

— Alan
Dr. Alan Wu
Head of Computational Pathology
GenLab Therapeutics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Alan Wu <alan.wu@genlab.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@genlab.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@genlab.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sealed-site readiness & next steps for air-gapped Private deployment - quick check-in

Alan / Rafael —

Thanks — quick answers so the procurement and field teams can move: 

- Hardware footprint: Pilot appliance is a 2U chassis with a software-defined node; it runs two primary GPUs (NVIDIA-class) and a small management NIC for out-of-band console. For a hardened air-gapped setup we recommend adding a 1U spare node (hot-swap capable) so you have immediate redundancy during upgrades. The 4U you mentioned will be sufficient if the spare node can sit adjacent (we can provide a simple rack diagram).

- LTO ingestion: Yes — we support LTO-7/LTO-8 ingestion workflows. Our field image delivery process for air-gapped sites supports chain-of-custody documentation and signed SHA256 manifests. The actual verification step can be performed using your HSM/KMS thumbprint verification; we'll provide the manifest format and verification script for your security team.

- Patch list: For the pilot we plan a narrowly scoped patch set: Redwood runtime (tokenizer/runtime libs), model weights (if any micro-updates), and OS security patches. We will not push non-security feature updates without a separate change window. We will deliver a pre-approved patch manifest and a rollback image that you store in your staging bay.

Procurement: attaching a preliminary BOM and a budgetary estimate (see attachment: site_inventory_genlab.xlsx sheet "BOM_estimate"). Rafael / Procurement — if you can confirm billing entity and PO process we’ll tee up a formal quote.

FieldOps call is confirmed: Wed 2026-08-25 10:00am ET — Zoom link to follow.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: redwood-airgap-handoff-checklist.pdf (example), site_inventory_genlab.xlsx (BOM_estimate)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Alan Wu <alan.wu@genlab.com>, Rafael Gomez <rafael.gomez@genlab.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:38:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sealed-site readiness & next steps for air-gapped Private deployment - quick check-in

Hi team —

Quick logistics / MAP items from the Redwood Ops perspective ahead of the FieldOps call: 
- I’ll pull a short FieldOps MOP draft with two options for acceptance testing: (A) smoke test (10 sample inferences, end-to-end) and (B) extended soak (24h at expected concurrency). Please indicate which you prefer for the pilot.
- We will highlight Dedicated fallback triggers in the MAP: unrecoverable hardware event (>4 hours), failed rollback validation, or security incident requiring rapid isolation. In those cases, Redwood can route traffic to a Dedicated pool while we coordinate image replacement on-site.
- On courier/chain-of-custody: we’ll add our preferred manifest template and custody tag examples to the Drive link (see related links).

Action items for FieldOps call: Rafael — confirm preferred acceptance test (Smoke / Soak), and procurement contact for quote routing. Soojin / Ben — please include a proposed Zoom link and the draft MAP before the call.

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
